name: atlas-citation-check
description: Check that the papers you cite exist and support the claims you cite them for.

interface.longDescription: Paste your writing and attach the papers you cite. Atlas checks that every reference exists and whether each paper supports the claim it's cited for, then gives you a report: what to fix first, the passage and page behind each claim, and a suggested rewrite. Open any finding to see the passage highlighted in the paper.
capabilities: Check that cited papers support claims
defaultPrompt: Do the citations in my paragraph exist, and do the papers say what I wrote?
Check whether every reference in this list is real.
Is this claim supported by the paper I attached?

positive.description: Check citations and claims in a paragraph against attached papers
positive.prompt:
Do the citations in my paragraph exist, and do the papers say what I wrote?

The most experienced agents benefited the most from AI assistance (Brynjolfsson et al., 2023). Replication effects were about a third the size of the originals (Open Science Collaboration, 2015).

References
Brynjolfsson, E., Li, D., & Raymond, L. R. (2023). Generative AI at work. NBER Working Paper 31161.
Open Science Collaboration. (2015). Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science. Science, 349(6251).
positive.expected_behavior: A report card shows both references found and both claims Not supported: the paper finds the least experienced agents benefited most, and replication effects were about half, not a third. Each finding shows the passage and page; Open full report shows the passage highlighted in the paper.

positive.description: Check whether references in a list exist
positive.prompt:
Do all of these references actually exist?
Brynjolfsson, E., Li, D., & Raymond, L. R. (2023). Generative AI at work. NBER Working Paper 31161.
Open Science Collaboration. (2016). Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science. Science, 349(6251).
Smith, J. (2021). AI tools and remote team output. Journal of Workplace Studies, 14(2), 55-70.
positive.expected_behavior: A report card lists each reference: Brynjolfsson found; Open Science Collaboration exists but the year differs (the record says 2015); Smith has no record found.

positive.description: A claim whose reference doesn't exist can't be checked, and says why
positive.prompt:
Is this claim supported? Remote teams using AI tools produced 20% more output (Smith, 2021).
Reference: Smith, J. (2021). AI tools and remote team output. Journal of Workplace Studies, 14(2), 55-70.
positive.expected_behavior: The report shows the claim as Can't check because the reference has no published record, and the reference as No record found.

positive.description: A supported claim with an attached paper
positive.prompt:
Does the attached paper support this sentence? AI assistance increased the number of chats agents resolved per hour by 14% on average (Brynjolfsson et al., 2023).
Reference: Brynjolfsson, E., Li, D., & Raymond, L. R. (2023). Generative AI at work. NBER Working Paper 31161.
positive.expected_behavior: The report shows the claim Supported, with the passage stating the 14% increase and its page.

positive.prompt: After the first test case's report appears, click Save to Atlas on the card and sign in with the review account.
positive.expected_behavior: A new Atlas project is created with the report as a note and the attached paper; the card shows Open in Atlas, which opens the project.

negative.description: Searching for papers is not a citation check
negative.prompt: Find me papers about generative AI and productivity.

negative.description: Summarising a paper is not a citation check
Writing text is not a citation check
negative.prompt: Write my literature review on AI and productivity.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: checks that references exist and that cited papers support the claims, with a report card and a full report beside the cited page.
